<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|148|THE GOSPEL|CHA. V.}}</noinclude>''30. Passing through the middes of them.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Christs body conteined in place aboue nature.}}Either by making him self inuisible, or also more wonderfully, penetrating the multitude and passing through them, as he did through the doore, his body either being without space of place, or with other bodies in one place. By al which and the like his doings mentioned in the Gospel, it is euident that he can alter and order his body as he list, aboue the natural conditions of a body.

''38. Simons wiues mother.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Apostles left their wiues.}}It is euident that Peter had a wife, but after his calling to be an Apostle, he leaft her, as S. Hierom writeth in many places ''ep. 34. c. 2. ad Iulianum. Li. 1. adu. Iouin''. See the Annot. ''Matth. 19, 29''.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. V.}}}}}}

{{c|''Hauing taught the people out of Peters ship, 4. he sheweth in a miraculous taking of fishes, how he vvil make him the fisher of men. 12. He cureth a leper by touching him, and sendeth him to the Priest in witnesse that he is not against Moyses. 15. The people flocking vnto him, he retireth into the vvildernesse. 17. To the Pharisees in a solemne assembly he proueth by a miracle his povver to remit sinnes in earth. 27. He defendeth his eating vvith sinners, as being the Physicion of soules, 33. and his not prescribing as yet of any fastes to his Disciples.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=5|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 4 Sunday after Pentecost.}}it came to passe, vvhen the multitudes pressed vpon him to heare the vvord of God, and him self stoode beside the lake of Genesareth. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=2}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 4, 18. Mar. 1, 16.''}}* And he savv tvvo shippes standing by the lake: and the fishers vvere gone dovvne, and vvashed their nettes. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=3}}† And he going vp into {{sup|‖}} one ship that vvas Simons, desired him to bring it backe a litle from the land. And sitting, he taught the multitudes out of the ship.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=4}}† And as he ceased to speake, he said to Simon, Launche forth into the deepe, and let loose your nettes to make a draught. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=5}}† And Simon ansvvering, said to him, Maister, labouring al the night, vve haue taken nothing: but in thy vvord I vvil let loose the nette. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=6}}† And vvhen they had done this, they inclosed {{sup|‖}} a very great multitude of fishes, and their nette vvas broken. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=7}}† And they {{sup|‖}} beckened to their fellovves that vvere in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came and filled both shippes, so that they did sinke. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=8}}† VVhich vvhen Simon Peter did see, he fel dovvne at {{sc|Iesvs}} knees, saying, Goe forth from me, because I am a sinful man, O Lord. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=9}}† For he vvas vvholy astonished and al that vvere vvith him, at the draught of fishes which they had taken. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=10}}† In like maner also Iames and Iohn the sonnes of Zebedee, vvho vvere Simons fellovves. And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to Simon, Feare not: from this time novv, {{sup|‖}} thou shalt be taking men. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=11}}† And hauing brought their shippes to land, leauing al things they folovved him.⊣

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 8, 2. Mar. 1, 40.''}}* And it came to passe, vvhen he vvas in one of the<noinclude>{{rh|||cities,}}</noinclude>
